*M.S. Student in Biostatistics, Columbia University*

I am a first-year M.S. student in Biostatistics (Public Health Data Science 
track) at the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health. I hold a 
B.S. in Applied Statistics from Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and 
Finance, and spent a summer studying at UC Berkeley.

## About Me

I am interested in using statistical and computational methods to understand 
how diseases develop and spread, and to turn large health datasets into 
evidence that can inform public health decisions. My background combines 
classical statistics (regression, time series, multivariate analysis) with 
machine learning, and I enjoy projects that bring the two together.

## Research Interests

* **Disease forecasting**: combining traditional time series models such as 
  ARIMA with deep learning models such as LSTM to predict infectious disease 
  trends
* **Epidemiology with large data**: analyzing large population datasets to 
  study how chronic conditions, such as diabetes and dementia, are related 
  across risk groups

## Selected Projects

* **Hepatitis B forecasting in China**: built ARIMA, LSTM, and hybrid 
  ARIMA-LSTM models on national HBV case data from 2011 to 2020 
  (undergraduate thesis)
* **Diabetes and dementia across BMI strata**: cross-sectional analysis of 
  over 400,000 records, with BMI groups defined using WHO standards
* **Interactive dashboard**: an [interactive dashboard](dashboard.html) built 
  with R, `plotly`, and `flexdashboard`
